A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NUFILT and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched despite terminology changes, additions, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and NLP merging results, component ablations, sensitivity studies, timing measurements, and empirical subspace analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds multimodal evaluations, additional baseline results, and stability/plasticity diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the specified LoRA initialization from zero A and Gaussian B in v1 to Gaussian A and zero B in v2. The null-space filter, optimization objective, and fusion procedure otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v2 retains the image-classification and GLUE coverage and adds multimodal evaluation on IconQA, ImageNet captioning, ScienceQA, and VizWiz-Caption. These extend evaluation to visual reasoning, scientific question answering, and captioning, including low-vision real-world inputs.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ISO-C, KNOTS-TIES, and TSV-M across all three CLIP backbones and all three task-group sizes. The overhead comparison also adds Task Arithmetic and OPCM in v2 Table 5. Existing vision and NLP comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces layer-averaged stability/plasticity losses and their harmonic mean, and reports total runtime alongside solving time. Its new multimodal evaluation specifies LLaVA-1.5-7B and alphabetical task order. Retained CLIP/GLUE protocols and budgets remain unchanged; multimodal scoring and training details are incompletely specified.

E4.justification: New Figure 5 directly examines the stability–plasticity balance across merging steps, comparing NUFILT with Task Arithmetic and OPCM. The efficiency analysis additionally distinguishes solving and total costs. Existing component ablations, rank sensitivity, and appendix subspace-alignment analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten vision task orders, seeds 42–51, and mean±standard-deviation reporting. Added vision baseline rows follow that practice. No changed repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline scores, multimodal results, surrogate-loss trajectories, and total-runtime measurements. Table 3 reports multimodal averages of 70.5 for NUFILT and 67.6 for OPCM. Table 5 reports 138.9 seconds total versus 18.4 seconds solving for 50-iteration NUFILT. Retained vision, NLP, ablation, and appendix scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix A correct the inconsistent use of affinity versus its complement. Appendix A.1 also replaces the square-root affinity expression in Eq. 25 with the mean squared cosine required by Eq. 5, repairs the exact-case statement, and explicitly completes the larger-subspace bound. The intended guarantee remains the same.

C1.justification: v1 claims that formulating transparency and fidelity is a novel contribution absent from prior work. v2 instead revisits the classical stability–plasticity balance and removes that contribution bullet from the introduction. This substantially narrows the claimed conceptual novelty, while retaining the alignment, method, and performance claims.

C2.justification: The efficiency discussion now acknowledges higher total cost from SVD despite lower solving time. v2 adds interpretations of the stability/plasticity diagnostics and hyperparameter behavior. Appendix D.1 removes the restriction to models below one billion parameters, while retaining the common-initialization and architecture limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access URL and Appendix B.4 guidance on rank selection, iteration counts, validation-based tuning, and reuse across architectures. Existing checkpoint sources and training recipes remain. The tuning advice does not establish that the reported experiments used a new tuning procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantial positioning against orthogonality-based methods, distinguishing data requirements and simultaneous versus sequential access to task vectors. It discusses additional work including Fang et al. (2025), Wang et al. (2023), and Xiong et al. (2024). The revised treatment of stability–plasticity also withdraws the earlier novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change throughout from transparency/fidelity to stability/plasticity. The abstract, Section 3.3, and efficiency discussion receive localized rewrites; acknowledgments and hyperparameter guidance are added. Most prose and the overall section hierarchy are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds multimodal Table 3 and diagnostic Figure 5, expands Table 1 with baseline rows, and expands the overhead table with total-time and comparator entries. Figure labels, conference headers, and float placement change. Existing appendix tables and alignment figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves rigor by repairing the affinity-proof inconsistency and exposing total runtime, making NUFILT's SVD cost assessable. Additional comparisons and multimodal results strengthen empirical support. These gains are tempered by sparse implementation and scoring details for new experiments, and Figure 5 does not support lower plasticity loss at every task as the accompanying discussion suggests.
